subject: Service assurance framework: credit schedule & latency carveouts
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@orionlytics.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: adjust SLA credit schedule + latency carveout for batch windows

Markus,

Thanks for taking this conversation — quick summary from our side attached (OrionLytics-SLA-redlines-v1.pdf). We're generally aligned with Redwood's standard 99.9% availability target, but two items are blockers for our procurement/legal team: 

1) Monthly credit cap: the current 25% cap exposes us to outsized risk for a small number of high-impact incidents. We request an increase to an uncapped or at least 50% monthly remedy ceiling while we run a pilot.

2) Latency SLO carveout for scheduled batch windows: our batch scoring jobs (large-batched inference) intentionally run in multi-hour windows and can tolerate higher tail latency during those windows. We need an explicit carveout so that those scheduled windows don't trigger availability/latency credits that are not operationally meaningful. Suggested language: "Batch processing windows (defined in customer MX schedule) may be excluded from latency SLO calculations provided Redwood meets pre-agreed throughput minimums."

Can Redwood propose concrete wording we can circulate with procurement? Also attaching a CSV with our typical batch windows and throughput (latency-sample-windows.csv).

If we can agree on those two points, procurement is ready to sign a 6-month reserved-capacity commitment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sanjay
Sanjay Mehta
Head of Platform, OrionLytics
S: +1 415 555 0198

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: adjust SLA credit schedule + latency carveout for batch windows

Sanjay — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. I've reviewed with legal and product; below are pragmatic options that maintain our operational guardrails while addressing OrionLytics' procurement concerns:

- Availability baseline: maintain 99.9% as standard.
- Monthly credit cap: for customers on reserved capacity we can increase the cap to 35% (from standard 25%) for the term of the commitment. Unlimited caps are tough operationally — they create open financial exposure for both sides. 35% is intended as a firm middle ground that legal has approved for enterprise pilots.
- Latency/Batch carveout: we can add explicit language that scheduled batch windows (customer-declared window up to N hours per calendar day) are excluded from latency-triggered credits provided Redwood meets a minimum throughput/processing SLA inside the window (we'll define numeric thresholds). The carveout will require the customer to publish the batch schedule and agree to a throughput minimum.

I'm attaching a proposed redline (SLA-proposal-Redwood-v2.pdf) with the 35% cap and example batch schedule language. If that looks good, we can surface the final with procurement and send a DocuSign link.

Next steps: 
- Sanjay: confirm you'd accept 35% cap with a 6-month reserved capacity commit at agreed pricing
- Laura/BG: legal + finance to run final numbers and approve redline

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Markus Klein
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Sanjay's ask and my reply. Quick internal points/asks: 

1) Commercial concession: I'd like to offer 35% monthly credit cap for a 6-month reserved capacity commitment at 10% below list for the pilot. That should be attractive to them and protects Redwood from open exposure.
2) Latency carveout: product suggests we define two carveouts: (a) scheduled batch windows <= 6 hours/day where customer publishes windows in advance; carveout applies only to p99 latency crediting, not availability. (b) an upper bound on batch window length (6 hours) to avoid perpetual carveouts.
3) Measurement & proof: require OrionLytics to publish scheduled windows and a throughput target (e.g., tokens/sec or jobs/hour). If throughput is not met, the carveout is void for that window.

Please review SLA-proposal-Redwood-v2.pdf and flag any legal/regulatory issues. Ben — can you run a quick financial exposure model if we accept 35% cap for a 6-month period on the estimated OrionLytics monthly run rate (see HubSpot deal id DL-2026-ORL-45)? Aditya — can infra validate that we can implement a throughput gating check in telemetry to mark windows as carved out?

Markus
